en: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, form Moala Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Ali,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘One could recognise the place of Prostration of Abu Abdullahasws by the aromatic smell of it’.

t: Chapter 48 – The Perfume
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) قال لي حبيبي جبرييل ( عليه السلام ) تطيب يوما و يوما لا و يوم الجمعه لا بد منه و لا تترك له .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Yasser,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said to me: ‘Mysaww beloved Jibraeelas said to me: ‘Apply perfume one day, and one day don’t, and the day of Friday is inevitable from it, and do not neglect it’.

t: Chapter 48 – The Perfume
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ليتطيب احدكم يوم الجمعه و لو من قاروره امراته .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Let each one of you apply perfume on the day of Friday, even if it is from a flask of his wife’.

t: Chapter 48 – The Perfume
ar: قال عثمان بن مظعون لرسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) قد اردت ان ادع الطيب و اشياء ذكرها فقال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) لا تدع الطيب فان الملايكه تستنشق ريح الطيب من المومن فلا تدع الطيب في كل جمعه .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, raising it,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Usman Bin Mazoun said to Rasool-Allahsaww, ‘I have intended to leave the perfume and certain things’, and he mentioned these. So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Do not leave the perfume, for the Angels desire the aromatic fragrances from the Believer, therefore do not leave the perfume during every Friday’.

t: Chapter 48 – The Perfume
ar: الطيب في الشارب من اخلاق الانبياء ( عليهم السلام ) و كرامه للكاتبين .
en: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The perfume in the moustache is from the mannerism of the Prophetsas and a prestige for the two Scribes (recording Angels)’.

t: Chapter 48 – The Perfume
ar: ما انفقت في الطيب فليس بسرف .
en: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Zakariyya Al Momin, raising it,  ‘Heasws said, ‘Whatever you spend regarding the perfume, so it is not an extravagance’.

t: Chapter 48 – The Perfume
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) طيب النساء ما ظهر لونه و خفي ريحه و طيب الرجال ما ظهر ريحه و خفي لونه .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Perfume of the women is what displays its colour and hides its smell, and a perfume of the men is what manifests its smell and hides its colour’.

t: Chapter 48 – The Perfume
ar: كان رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ينفق في الطيب اكثر مما ينفق في الطعام .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Suleyman Bin Muhammad Al Khash’amy, from Ishaq Al Taweel Al Attar,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww used to spend regarding the perfume more than what hesaww used to spend regarding the food’.

t: Chapter 49 – Abhorrence of rejecting the perfume
ar: سالته عن الرجل يرد الطيب قال لا ينبغي له ان يرد الكرامه .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the man who rejects the perfume. Heasws said: ‘It is not befitting that he rejects the prestige’.

t: Chapter 49 – Abhorrence of rejecting the perfume
ar: اتي امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) بدهن و قد كان ادهن فادهن فقال انا لا نرد الطيب .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws was given anointing oil, and heasws used to anoint. So heasws anointed and said: ‘Iasws do not reject the perfume’.

t: Chapter 49 – Abhorrence of rejecting the perfume
ar: دخلت علي ابي الحسن ( عليه السلام ) فاخرج الي مخزنه فيها مسك و قال خذ من هذا فاخذت منه شييا فتمسحت به فقال اصلح و اجعل في لبتك منه قال فاخذت منه قليلا فجعلته في لبتي فقال لي اصلح فاخذت منه ايضا فمكث في يدي منه شي‏ء صالح فقال لي اجعل في لبتك ففعلت ثم قال قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) لا يابي الكرامه الا حمار قال قلت ما معني ذلك قال الطيب و الوساده و عد اشياء.
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said,  ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassanasws, so heasws brought out to me a perfume box in which was musk, and said: ‘Take from this’. So I took something from it, and I applied with it. So heasws said: ‘More, and make it to be in your chest from it’. So I took a little from it and made it to be in my chest. So heasws said to me: ‘More’. So I took from it again, and there remained something from it in my hand. So heasws said to me: ‘Make it to be in your chest’. So I did it. Then heasws said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘No one refuses the prestige except for a donkey’. I said, ‘What is the meaning of that?’ Heasws said: ‘The perfume, and the pillow and a number of things’.

t: Chapter 49 – Abhorrence of rejecting the perfume
ar: النبي ( صلي الله عليه واله ) كان لا يرد الطيب و الحلواء .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather,  (It has been narrated) from Aliasws that: ‘The Prophetsaww never used to reject the perfume and the sweets’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: دخلت علي ابي جعفر ( عليه السلام ) و هو في بيت منجد و عليه قميص رطب و ملحفه مصبوغه قد اثر الصبغ علي عاتقه فجعلت انظر الي البيت و انظر الي هييته فقال يا حكم ما تقول في هذا فقلت و ما عسيت ان اقول و انا اراه عليك و اما عندنا فانما يفعله الشاب المرهق فقال لي يا حكم من حرم زينه الله التي اخرج لعباده و الطيبات من الرزق و هذا مما اخرج الله لعباده فاما هذا البيت الذي تري فهو بيت المراه و انا قريب العهد بالعرس و بيتي البيت الذي تعرف .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Mayassar, from Al Hakam Bin Uteyba who said,  ‘I went over to Abu Ja’farasws and heasws was in a recently furbished room, and upon himasws was a dyed shirt and a dyed sheet, the effects of the dye being upon his shoulders. So heasws went on to look at the room and looking at its furnishings, so heasws said: ‘O Hakam! What are you saying regarding this?’ So I said, ‘And what I was about to say, and I saw it upon youasws, and as for with us, so it is rather the worn-out youth who are doing it’. So heasws said to me: ‘O Hakam! [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? And this is from what Allahazwj has Brought forth for Hisazwj servants. So As for this room which you see, so it is the ladies chamber, and Iasws am very close to the time of the wedding, and myasws room is the room which you know’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: لا باس بلبس المعصفر .
en: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Muhammad Bin Humran and Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,  (It has been narrated) from one of the twoasws (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said: ‘There is no problem with wearing the dyed (clothes)’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: رايت علي ابي جعفر ( عليه السلام ) ثوبا معصفرا فقال اني تزوجت امراه من قريش .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, fromhis father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad, from Zurara who said,  ‘I saw upon Abu Ja’farasws some dyed clothes, so heasws said: ‘Iasws (just) married a woman from Qureysh’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) نهاني رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) عن لبس ثياب الشهره و لا اقول نهاكم عن لباس المعصفر المفدم .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Al Qaddah,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade measws from wearing the defaming clothes, and Iasws am not saying hesaww forbade you all from wearing the dyed, the vibrant-coloured’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: يكره المفدم الا للعروس .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man,  Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘The vibrant-coloured (clothing) is disliked except for the wedding’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: انا نلبس المعصفرات و المضرجات .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘weasws wear the dyed clothes and the reddened (vibrant-coloured) ones’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: دخلت علي ابي جعفر ( عليه السلام ) و عليه ملحفه حمراء جديده شديده الحمره فتبسمت حين دخلت فقال كاني اعلم لم ضحكت ضحكت من هذا الثوب الذي هو علي ان الثقفيه اكرهتني عليه و انا احبها فاكرهتني علي لبسها ثم قال انا لا نصلي في هذا و لا تصلوا في المشبع المضرج قال ثم دخلت عليه و قد طلقها فقال سمعتها تبرا من علي ( عليه السلام ) فلم يسعني ان امسكها و هي تبرا منه .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, form Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Bureyd, from Malik Bin Ayn who said,  ‘I went over to Abu Ja’farasws and upon himasws was a red sheet, new, intensely red. So I smiled when I entered, so heasws said: ‘It is as if Iasws know why you are laughing. You are laughing at this cloth, which is upon measws. It was the Saqafiyya woman who compelled measws over it, and Iasws love her, so she compelled measws upon wearing it’. Then heasws said: ‘Weasws do not Pray in this nor do weasws Pray in vibrant colours’.  He (the narrator) said, ‘Then I went over to himasws, and heasws had divorced her, so heasws said: ‘Iasws heard her disavowing from Aliasws, so there was no leeway for measws that Iasws should keep her and she disavowed from himasws’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: كان ابو جعفر ( عليه السلام ) يلبس المعصفر و المنير .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,  ‘Abu Ja’farasws used to wear the dyed and the radiant (clothes)’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) كانت له ملحفه مورسه يلبسها في اهله حتي يردع علي جسده و قال قال ابو جعفر ( عليه السلام ) كنا نلبس المعصفر في البيت .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Al Qaddah,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that Rasool-Allahsaww had a sheet made in Wars (a city), wearing it among hissaww family until heasws turned it upon hissaww body’.  And he (the narrator) said, ‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Weasws wear the dyed clothes in the house’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: صبغنا البهرمان و صبغ بني اميه الزعفران .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Ourasws dyeing is Al-Bahramaan, and the dyeing of the Clan of Umayya is the saffron’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: رايت علي ابي الحسن ( عليه السلام ) طيلسانا ازرق .
en: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin ZIyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus who said,  ‘I saw a blue pallium upon Abu Al-Hassanasws’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: رايت علي ابي الحسن ( عليه السلام ) ثوبا عدسيا .
en: Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ali who said,  ‘I saw a seed-shaped cloth upon Abu Al-Hassanasws’.

t: Chapter 5 – Wearing the dyed clothes
ar: دخلت علي ابي جعفر ( عليه السلام ) انا و صاحب لي و اذا هو في بيت منجد و عليه ملحفه ورديه و قد حف لحيته و اكتحل فسالناه عن مسايل فلما قمنا قال لي يا حسن قلت لبيك قال اذا كان غدا فايتني انت و صاحبك فقلت نعم جعلت فداك فلما كان من الغد دخلت عليه و اذا هو في بيت ليس فيه الا حصير و اذا عليه قميص غليظ ثم اقبل علي صاحبي فقال يا اخا اهل البصره انك دخلت علي امس و انا في بيت المراه و كان امس يومها و البيت بيتها و المتاع متاعها فتزينت لي علي ان اتزين لها كما تزينت لي فلا يدخل قلبك شي‏ء فقال له صاحبي جعلت فداك قد كان و الله دخل في قلبي شي‏ء فاما الان فقد و الله اذهب الله ما كان و علمت ان الحق فيما قلت .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Zayyat Al Basry who said,  ‘I and a companion of mine went to Abu Ja’farasws, and heasws was is a recently refurbished room, and upon himasws was a pink sheet, and had trimmed hisasws beard and applied kohl. So we asked himasws certain questions. So when we arose, heasws said to me: ‘O Hassan!’ I said, ‘At yourasws service!’ Heasws said: ‘When it is the morning, so come to me, you and your companion’. So I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for youasws’.  So when it was the morning, we went over to himasws, and heasws was in a room in which there was nothing except for a mat and upon himasws was a coarse shirt. Then heasws faced towards my companions, so heasws said: ‘O brother of the people of Al-Basra! You came over to measws yesterday and Iasws was in the wife’s chamber, and yesterday was her day, and the room was her room, and the chattels were her chattels. So she adorned for measws upon (the condition) that Iasws would adorn for her just as she had adorned for measws, therefore do not let anything enter your heart’. So my companion said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! By Allahazwj, there had entered something into my heart, so as for now, so by Allahazwj, Allahazwj has Removed what was (in my heart), and I know that the truth is in what youasws say’.

t: Chapter 50 – Types of perfumes
ar: سمعت ابا عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) يقول الطيب المسك و العنبر و الزعفران و العود .
en: Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Abdul Ghaffar who said,  ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The perfume is the musk, and the Amber, and the saffron, and the Oud (Aloe wood)’.

t: Chapter 51 – The origination of the perfume
ar: لما اهبط ادم ( عليه السلام ) من الجنه علي الصفا و حواء علي المروه و قد كانت امتشطت في الجنه بطيب من طيب الجنه فلما صارت في الارض قالت ما ارجو من المشط و انا مسخوط علي فحلت عقيصتها فانتثر من مشطتها التي كانت امتشطت بها في الجنه فطارت به الريح فالقت اكثره بالهند فلذلك صار العطر بالهند . عده من اصحابنا عن احمد بن ابي عبد الله عن علي بن حسان مثله . قال و في حديث اخر فحلت عقيصتها فارسل الله علي ما كان فيها من ذلك الطيب ريحا فهبت في المشرق و المغرب فاصل الطيب من ذلك .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When Adamas descended from the Paradise upon Al-Safa and Hawwaas upon the Marwa, and sheas used to comb in the Paradise with a perfume from the perfumes of the Paradise. So when sheas came to be in the earth, sheas said: ‘How hopeful Ias am from the combing and Ias am loathsome of myas hair’. So sheas loosened heras braids, so there scattered from her combing which sheas used to comb with in the Paradise, and the wind carried it and cast most of it in India. Thus, it is due to that, came to be the perfume in India’.  A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Adullah, from Ali Bin Hassan – similar to it. He (the narrator) said, ‘And in another Hadeeth - :  ‘Sheas loosened her braids, so Allahazwj Sent upon what was therein, from that perfume, a wind, so it descended in the eat and the west. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that’.

t: Chapter 51 – The origination of the perfume
ar: سالته عن اصل الطيب من اي شي‏ء هو فقال اي شي‏ء يقوله الناس قلت يزعمون ان ادم هبط من الجنه و علي راسه اكليل فقال قد كان و الله اشغل من ان يكون علي راسه اكليل ثم قال ان حواء امتشطت في الجنه بطيب من طيب الجنه قبل ان تواقعها الخطييه فلما هبطت الي الارض حلت عقيصتها فارسل الله تعالي علي ما كان فيها ريحا فهبت به في المشرق و المغرب فاصل الطيب من ذلك .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Yahya, from Ali Al Qaseyr, from a man,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked Himasws about the origination of the perfume, from which thing is it?’ So heasws said: ‘Which thing are the people saying?’ I said, ‘They are alleging that Adamas descended from the Paradise and upon hisas head was a crown’. So heasws said: ‘Heas was too pre-occupied that there would happen to be a crown upon hisas head’.  Then heasws said: ‘Hawwaas used to comb in the Paradise with a perfume from the perfumes of the Paradise before the occurrence of heras error. So when sheas descended to the earth, sheas loosened heras hair, so Allahazwj the High Sent upon what was therein, a wind, so it descended with it in the east and the west. Thus, the origination of the perfume is from that’.

t: Chapter 51 – The origination of the perfume
ar: ان الله تعالي لما اهبط ادم طفق يخصف من ورق الجنه فطار عنه لباسه الذي كان عليه من حلل الجنه فالتقط ورقه فستر بها عورته فلما هبط عبقت رايحه تلك الورقه بالهند بالنبت فصار الطيب في الارض من سبب تلك الورقه التي عبقت بها رايحه الجنه فمن هناك الطيب بالهند لان الورقه هبت عليها ريح الجنوب فادت رايحتها الي المغرب لانها احتملت رايحه الورقه في الجو فلما ركدت الريح بالهند عبق باشجارهم و نبتهم فكان اول بهيمه رتعت من تلك الورقه ظبي المسك فمن هناك صار المسك في سره الظبي لانه جري رايحه النبت في جسده و في دمه حتي اجتمعت في سره الظبي .
en: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza,  (It has been narrated) from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When Allahazwj the Exalted Caused Adamas to descend from the Paradise, heas started covering himselfas from a leaf of the Paradise, and hisas clothes flew away from himas, which used to be upon himas from the garments of the Paradise. So heas cut off a leaf and veiled hisas nakedness with it.   So when heas descended, the aroma of that leaf remained at India with the vegetation. So the perfume came to be in the earth from the cause of that leaf upon which remained the aroma of the Paradise. Thus, from here on the perfume is at India, because upon the leaf fell the south wind, so its aroma led to the west because it carried the aroma of the leaf in the atmosphere. So when the wind stagnated at India, it remained in its trees, and its vegetation. So the first animal which grazed the musk from that leaf was a deer. Thus, from over there the musk came to be in the navel of the deer flowing the aroma of the vegetation in its body, and in its blood, gathering in the navel of the deer’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: سمعت ابا الحسن ( عليه السلام ) يقول كانت لعلي بن الحسين ( عليه السلام ) اشبيدانه رصاص معلقه فيها مسك فاذا اراد ان يخرج و لبس ثيابه تناولها و اخرج منها فتمسح به .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa who said,  ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassanasws saying: ‘There used to be for Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws a lead container wherein was musk. So whenever heasws wanted to go out and wear hisasws clothes, heasws would take it and extract from it, so heasws would apply with it’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) كان يتطيب بالمسك حتي يري وبيصه في مفارقه .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abu Al Bakhtary,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that Rasool-Allahsaww used to perfume with the musk to the extent that its marks could be seen in hissaww (finger) joints’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: كانت لرسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ممسكه اذا هو توضا اخذها بيده و هي رطبه فكان اذا خرج عرفوا انه رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) برايحته .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There used to be for Rasool-Allahsaww a musk holder. Whenever hesaww performed ablution, hesaww would grab it with hissaww hands while wet. So when hesaww went out, it would be recognised that hesaww is Rasool-Allahsaww by its fragrance’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: اخرج الي ابو الحسن ( عليه السلام ) مخزنه فيها مسك من عتيده ابنوس فيها بيوت كلها مما يتخذها النساء .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said,  ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws brought out to me a perfume box of ebony interior in which was musk, compartmentalised from what the women would take’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: سالت ابا عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) عن المسك هل يجوز اشتمامه فقال انا لنشمه .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Muttalab Bin Ziyad, from Abu Bukr Bin Abdullah Al Ashary who said,  ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the musk, ‘Is it allowed to smell it?’ So heasws said: ‘Weasws do smell it’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: كانت لعلي بن الحسين ( عليه السلام ) قاروره مسك في مسجده فاذا دخل للصلاه اخذ منه فتمسح به .
en: From him, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from his father, from his father, from his uncle Is’haq Bin Abdullah, from his father Abdullah Bin Al Haris who said,  ‘There used to be for Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws, a flask of musk in hisasws Masjid. So whenever heasws entered for the Prayer, heasws would take from it, so heasws would wipe with it’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: كان يري وبيص المسك في مفرق رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) .
en: From him, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from one of our companions,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws having said: ‘The marks of the musk could be seen in the (finger) joints of Rasool-Allahsaww’.

t: Chapter 52 – The Musk
ar: سالته عن المسك في الدهن ا يصلح قال اني لاصنعه في الدهن و لا باس . و روي انه لا باس بصنع المسك في الطعام .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali,  (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws, from his brotherasws Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the musk in the anointing (oiling/massaging) is it correct?’ Heasws said: ‘Iasws apply it in the anointing and there is no problem’. And it is reported that there is no problem with making the musk to be in the food.

t: Chapter 53 – Al-Ghaliya (A type of perfume)
ar: قلت لابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) اني اعامل التجار فاتهيا للناس كراهه ان يروا بي خصاصه فاتخذ الغاليه فقال يا اسحاق ان القليل من الغاليه يجزي و كثيرها سواء من اتخذ من الغاليه قليلا دايما اجزاه ذلك قال اسحاق و انا اشتري منها في السنه بعشره دراهم فاكتفي بها و ريحها ثابت طول الدهر .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, said,  ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I work with the business people, so I make myself pleasant for the people not liking that they should see me as a destitute, so I take Al-Ghaliya’. So heasws said: ‘O Is’haq! A little from Al-Ghaliya suffices and a lot of it is the same. The one who takes a little Ghaliya all the time, that would suffice for him’. I’shaq said, ‘And I bought from it during the year with ten Dirhams, so I sufficed myself with it, and its aroma was affirmed for a long duration’.

t: Chapter 53 – Al-Ghaliya (A type of perfume)
ar: امرني ابو الحسن الرضا ( عليه السلام ) فعملت له دهنا فيه مسك و عنبر فامرني ان اكتب في قرطاس ايه الكرسي و ام الكتاب و المعوذتين و قوارع من القران و اجعله بين الغلاف و القاروره ففعلت ثم اتيته به فتغلف به و انا انظر اليه .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said,  ‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws ordered me, so I made a flask for himasws in which was musk, and Amber. So heasws ordered me that I should write down in a paper the Verse of the Chair [2:255], and the Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha), and Al-Mawazatain (Chapters 113 & 114), and certain Verses from the Quran, and make these to be in between the covering and the flask. So I did it, then I came over to himasws with it, and heasws placed it in a covering, and I was looking at himasws’.

t: Chapter 53 – Al-Ghaliya (A type of perfume)
ar: خرج علي بن الحسين ( عليه السلام ) ليله و عليه جبه خز و كساء خز قد غلف لحيته بالغاليه فقالوا في هذه الساعه في هذه الهييه فقال اني اريد ان اخطب الحور العين الي الله عز و جل في هذه الليله . سهل بن زياد عن علي بن اسباط عن مولي لبني هاشم عن محمد بن جعفر مثله .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from a slave of the Clan of hashimas, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far Bin Muhammad who said,  ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws came out one night and upon himasws was a robe of khazz and a cloak of khazz, and heasws had covered hisasws beard with Al-Ghaliya. So they (people) said, ‘At this time and in this beard?’ So heasws said: ‘I wanted to address the Maiden Hourie to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic during this night’.  Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from a slave of the Clan of Hashimas, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far – similar to it.

t: Chapter 53 – Al-Ghaliya (A type of perfume)
ar: قلت لابي جعفر الثاني ( عليه السلام ) ما تقول في المسك فقال ان ابي امر فعمل له مسك في بان بسبعمايه درهم فكتب اليه الفضل بن سهل يخبره ان الناس يعيبون ذلك فكتب اليه يا فضل ا ما علمت ان يوسف ( عليه السلام ) و هو نبي كان يلبس الديباج مزررا بالذهب و يجلس علي كراسي الذهب و لم ينقص ذلك من حكمته شييا قال ثم امر فعملت له غاليه باربعه الاف درهم .
en: From him, from Abu Al Qasim Al Kufy, from the one who narrated it, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed Al Kirmany who said,  ‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws the 2nd, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the musk?’ So heasws said: ‘Myasws fatherasws ordered for musk to be made for himasws in a container, for seven hundred Dirhams. So Al-Fazl Bin Sahl wrote to himasws, informing himasws that the people are refusing that. So heasws wrote to him: ‘O Fazl! But do you not know that Yusufas, and heas was a Prophetas, used to wear the brocade buttoned with the gold, and would sit upon a chair of gold, and that did not reduce anything from hisas wisdom?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So I made Ghaliya for himas for four thousand Dirhams’.

t: Chapter 53 – Al-Ghaliya (A type of perfume)
ar: ان علي بن الحسين ( عليه السلام ) استقبله مولي له في ليله بارده و عليه جبه خز و مطرف خز و عمامه خز و هو متغلف بالغاليه فقال له جعلت فداك في مثل هذه الساعه علي هذه الهييه الي اين قال فقال الي مسجد جدي رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) اخطب الحور العين الي الله عز و جل .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed, from one of his companions,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws met a slave of hisasws on a cold night and upon himasws was a rod of khazz, a gown of khazz, and a turban of khazz, and heasws had applied Al-Ghaliya. So he said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! In a time like this, upon this beard, where to (are youasws going)?’ So heasws said: ‘To the Masjid of myasws grandfathersaww Rasool-Allahsaww, to address the Maiden Hourie to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’.

t: Chapter 54 – Al-Khalouq (A type of perfume)
ar: سالت ابا جعفر ( عليه السلام ) عن الخلوق اخذ منه قال لا باس و لكن لا احب ان تدوم عليه .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,  ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about Al-Khalouq, taking from it’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it, but Iasws do not like it that you are perpetually upon it’.

t: Chapter 54 – Al-Khalouq (A type of perfume)
ar: لا باس ان تمس الخلوق في الحمام او تمس به يديك من الشقاق تداويهما به و لا احب ادمانه و قال لا باس ان يتخلق الرجل و لكن لا يبيت متخلقا .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘There is no problem if you wipe Al-Khalouq in the bathhouse, or wipe your hands with it from the cracks (dry hands) to cure by it, and Iasws do not like making a habit of it’. And heasws said: ‘There is no problem that the man applies Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied it’.

t: Chapter 54 – Al-Khalouq (A type of perfume)
ar: لا باس ان تمس الخلوق في الحمام او تمسح به يدك تداوي به و لا احب ادمانه .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,  ‘Heasws said: ‘There is no problem if you wipe Al-Khalouq in the bathhouse, or wipe your hands with it to cure by it (dryness of hands), and Iasws do not like being habitual of it’.

t: Chapter 54 – Al-Khalouq (A type of perfume)
ar: سمعت ابا عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) يقول انه ليعجبني الخلوق .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from a man, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said,  ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Iasws love Al-Khalouq’.

t: Chapter 54 – Al-Khalouq (A type of perfume)
ar: لا باس ان يتخلق الرجل لامراته و لكن لا يبيت متخلقا .
en: Humey Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Aban, from a man who had affirmed it,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws havign said: ‘There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq for his wife, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq’.

t: Chapter 54 – Al-Khalouq (A type of perfume)
ar: لا باس بان يتخلق الرجل و لكن لا يبيت متخلقا .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Aban, from Al Fazeyl, from a man,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘There is no problem if the man were to apply Al-Khalouq, but he should not sleep overnight having applied Al-Khalouq’.

t: Chapter 55 – The Incense
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) يبقي ريح العود التي في البدن اربعين يوما و يبقي ريح عود المطراه عشرين يوما .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al ja’fary, from one of his companions, raising it, said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The aroma of Al-Oud which is in the body remains for forty days, and the aroma of Oud in the perfumes remains for twenty days’.

t: Chapter 55 – The Incense
ar: ينبغي للرجل ان يدخن ثيابه اذا كان يقدر .
en: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘It is befitting for the man that he does incense whenever he is able to’.

t: Chapter 55 – The Incense
ar: خرج الي ابو الحسن ( عليه السلام ) فوجدت منه رايحه التجمير .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said,  ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws came out to me, so I found from himasws an aroma of Al-Tajmeer (incense)’.

t: Chapter 55 – The Incense
ar: دخلت مع ابي الحسن ( عليه السلام ) الحمام فلما خرج الي المسلخ دعا بمجمره فتجمر بها ثم قال جمروا مرازم قال قلت من اراد ان ياخذ نصيبه ياخذ قال نعم .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Murazam who said,  ‘I entered the bathhouse along with Abu Al-Hassanasws. So when we came to the dressing room, heasws called for the incense burner so heasws applied the incense vapour with it, then said: ‘Apply the incense O Murazam! I said, ‘The one who want that he takes his share, can he take it?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.

t: Chapter 55 – The Incense
ar: احمد كان نساء ابي الحسن ( عليه السلام ) اذا تبخرن اخذن نواه من نوي الصيحاني ممسوحه من التمر منقاه التمر و القشاره فالقينها علي النار قبل البخور فاذا دخنت النواه ادني الدخان رمين النواه و تبخرن من بعد و كن يقلن هو اعبق و اطيب للبخور و كن يامرن بذلك .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan,  (It has been narrated) from Ahmad Bin Abu Khalaf, a slave of Abu Al-Hassanasws, and heasws had bought his father, and his mother, and his brother, so heasws had freed them, and heasws had contracted Ahmad and made him hisasws butler. So Ahmad said, ‘When the wives of Abu Al-Hassanasws incensed, they took a type from a type of Al-Saykhani date, unrefined dates, and the peels, so they would cast these upon the fire before the incense. So when the dates smoked a little smoke, they threw the dates and burnt the incense from afterwards, and it tended to hand and be more remaining, and more aromatic for the vapour, and they used to instruct with these’.

t: Chapter 56 – The Oiling (Massaging)
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) الدهن يلين البشره و يزيد في الدماغ و يسهل مجاري الماء و يذهب القشف و يسفر اللون .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The oiling (massaging) smoothens the person (skin) and increases in the brain, and eases the flow of the water (urination), and removes the scaling (dryness of the skin), and shines the complexion’.

t: Chapter 56 – The Oiling (Massaging)
ar: الدهن يذهب بالسوء .
en: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The oiling (massaging) removes the evil’.

t: Chapter 56 – The Oiling (Massaging)
ar: الدهن يظهر الغني .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The oiling manifests the riches’.

t: Chapter 56 – The Oiling (Massaging)
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) الدهن يلين البشره و يزيد في الدماغ القوه و يسهل مجاري الماء و هو يذهب بالقشف و يحسن اللون .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The oiling (massaging) smoothens the person (skin), and increases in the brain power, and eases the flow of the water (urination), and it removes the scaling (dryness of the skin) and improves the complexion’.

t: Chapter 56 – The Oiling (Massaging)
ar: دهن الليل يجري في العروق و يروي البشره و يبيض الوجه .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Hamza,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The oiling (massaging) at night flows in the veins and it irrigates the person (skin), and whitens the face’.

t: Chapter 56 – The Oiling (Massaging)
ar: اذا اخذت الدهن علي راحتك فقل اللهم اني اسالك الزين و الزينه و المحبه و اعوذ بك من الشين و الشنان و المقت ثم اجعله علي يافوخك ابدا بما بدا الله به .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Bahr, from Mihzam Al Asady,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever you take the oil upon your convenience, so say, ‘O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj for the grace and the beauty and the love, and I seek Refuge with Youazwj from the disgrace, and the ugliness and the detestation’.

t: Chapter 56 – The Oiling (Massaging)
ar: من دهن مومنا كتب الله له بكل شعره نورا يوم القيامه .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Daqqan, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Bashir the masseur,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who oils (massages) a Believer, Allahazwj Writes for him with every hair, a radiance on the Day of Judgement’.

t: Chapter 57 – Abhorrence of being habitual of the oiling (massaging)
ar: لا يدهن الرجل كل يوم يري الرجل شعثا لا يري متزلقا كانه امراه .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The man should not oil (massage) every day. The man should look shaggier and he should not look smooth like a woman’.

t: Chapter 57 – Abhorrence of being habitual of the oiling (massaging)
ar: قلت لابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) اخالط اهل المروءه من الناس و قد اكتفي من الدهن باليسير فاتمسح به كل يوم فقال ما احب لك ذلك فقلت يوم و يوم لا فقال و ما احب لك ذلك قلت يوم و يومين لا فقال الجمعه الي الجمعه يوم و يومين .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,  ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I intermingle with the manly from the people and I have sufficed from the oil by the little bit, so I wipe with it every day’. So heasws said: ‘Iasws do not like that for you’. So I said, ‘A day and not a day (alternatively)?’ So heasws said: ‘Iasws do not like that for you’. I said, ‘One day, and not for two days?’ So heasws said: ‘The Friday to the Friday, one day or two days’.

t: Chapter 57 – Abhorrence of being habitual of the oiling (massaging)
ar: قلت لابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) في كم ادهن قال في كل سنه مره فقلت اذن يري الناس بي خصاصه فلم ازل اماكسه فقال ففي كل شهر مره لم يزدني عليها .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Jareer who said,  ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘How much shall I oil (massage)?’ Heasws said: ‘Once during every year’. So I said, ‘Then the people would look at me as a destitute’. So I did not cease bargaining with himasws, so heasws said: ‘So in every month, once’, and heasws did not increase over it’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: قال البنفسج سيد ادهانكم .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The violet (oil) is the chief of your (massaging) oils’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: اهديت الي ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) بغله فصرعت الذي ارسلت بها معه فامته فدخلنا المدينه فاخبرنا ابا عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) فقال ا فلا اسعطتموه بنفسجا فاسعط بالبنفسج فبرا ثم قال يا عقبه ان البنفسج بارد في الصيف حار في الشتاء لين علي شيعتنا يابس علي عدونا لو يعلم الناس ما في البنفسج قامت اوقيته بدينار .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Zayd Al Razy, from his father, from Salih Bin Uqba, from his father who said,  ‘I gifted a mule to Abu Abdullahasws, so it dislodged the rider which I had sent along with it.  So we went over to himasws and we entered Al-Medina. So we informed Abu Abdullahasws and heasws said: ‘Why don’t you make it sniff the violet (oil)?’ So I made it to sniff violet (oil) and it was cured. Then heasws said: ‘O Uqba! The violet (oil) is cold in the summer and hot in the winter, soft upon ourasws Shias, dry upon ourasws enemies. Had the people known what was in the violet (oil), they would have evaluated one Owqiya (a unit of measurement) of it, for one Dinar’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) ما ياتينا من ناحيتكم شي‏ء احب الينا من البنفسج .
en: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There has not come to usasws from your area anything more beloved to usasws than the violet (oil)’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: مثل البنفسج في الادهان مثلنا في الناس .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba, from Asbaat Bin Salim, from Israil Bin Abu Asama Baya’a Al Zaty,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The example of the violet (oil) among the (massaging) oils is like ourasws example among the people’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: فضل البنفسج علي الادهان كفضل الاسلام علي الاديان نعم الدهن البنفسج ليذهب بالداء من الراس و العينين فادهنوا به .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The merit of the violet (oil) upon the (massaging) oils is like the merit of Al-Islam upon the (rest of the) religions. The best of the (massaging) oils is the violet (oil) for removing the illnesses from the head, and the eyes, therefore oil (massage) with it’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: كنت عند ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) فدخل عليه مهزم فقال لي ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) ادع لنا الجاريه تجينا بدهن و كحل فدعوت بها فجاءت بقاروره بنفسج و كان يوما شديد البرد فصب مهزم في راحته منها ثم قال جعلت فداك هذا بنفسج و هذا البرد الشديد فقال و ما باله يا مهزم فقال ان متطببينا بالكوفه يزعمون ان البنفسج بارد فقال هو بارد في الصيف لين حار في الشتاء .
en: Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer who said,  ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so Mahzam came over to himasws. So Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘Call the maid for usasws to bring usasws the (massaging) oil and kohl’. So I called her with it and she came over with a flask of violet (oil), and it was an intensely cold day. So Mihzam poured in his hand from it, then said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! This is violet (oil), and this is extremely cold’. So heasws said: ‘And what is the matter with it, O Mihzam?’ So he said, ‘Our physicians at Al-Kufa are alleging that the violet (oil) is cold?’ So heasws said: ‘It is cold in the summer, and is soft and hot in the winter’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) استعطوا بالبنفسج فان رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) قال لو يعلم الناس ما في البنفسج لحسوه حسوا .
en: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from al Qasim Bin yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Sniff the violet (oil), for Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Had the people known what was in the violet (oil), they would have drunk it (like) soup (slurping)’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: دهن البنفسج يرزن الدماغ .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Sowqa,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Oiling with the violet (oil) calms the brain’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: دهن الحاجبين بالبنفسج يذهب بالصداع .
en: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, raising it,  ‘Heasws said: ‘Oiling the two eyebrows removes the headache’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: مثل البنفسج في الدهن كمثل شيعتنا في الناس .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Usman Bin Isa, from Khalid Bin Najeeh,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘An example of the violet (oil) among the oils is like an example of ourasws Shias among the people’.

t: Chapter 58 – The Violet oil
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) اكسروا حر الحمي بالبنفسج .
en: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Break the heat of the fever with the violet (oil)’.

t: Chapter 59 – Gillyflower oil
ar: ذكر دهن البنفسج فزكاه ثم قال و ان الخيري لطيف .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ali Al Ash’ary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Al Jabbar, altogether from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from the one who mentioned it,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws spoke mentioning the violet (oil), so heasws praised it, then said: ‘And the gillyflower oil is gentle’.

t: Chapter 59 – Gillyflower oil
ar: رايت ابا الحسن ( عليه السلام ) يدهن بالخيري فقال لي ادهن فقلت له اين انت عن البنفسج و قد روي فيه عن ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) قال اكره ريحه قال قلت له فاني كنت اكره ريحه و اكره ان اقول ذلك لما بلغني فيه عن ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) قال لا باس .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, and Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said,  ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassanasws oiling with the gillyflower oil, so heasws said to me: ‘Oil (yourself)’. So I said to himasws, ‘Where do youasws stand about the violet (oil) and what has been reported with regards to it, from Abu Abdullahasws?’ Heasws said: ‘Iasws dislike its smell’. I said to himasws, ‘So I (also) did not like its smell and I did not like to say that to youasws due to what has reached me with regards to it from Abu Abdullahasws’. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’.

t: Chapter 6 – Wearing the black
ar: كان رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) يكره السواد الا في ثلاث الخف و العمامه و الكساء .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, raising it, said,  ‘Rasool-Allahsaww used to dislike (wearing) the black except regarding three (apparels) – the socks, and the turban, and the cloak’.

t: Chapter 6 – Wearing the black
ar: كنت عند ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) بالحيره فاتاه رسول ابي جعفر الخليفه يدعوه فدعا بممطر احد وجهيه اسود و الاخر ابيض فلبسه ثم قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) اما اني البسه و انا اعلم انه لباس اهل النار .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour who said,  ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws at Al-Hira, a messenger of Abu Ja’far the Caliph came over calling himasws. So heasws called for the rain-coat, one aspect of it being black and the other white, so heasws wore it. Then Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘But, Iasws am wearing it and Iasws know that it is a clothing of the inhabitants of the Fire’.

t: Chapter 6 – Wearing the black
ar: رايت علي بن الحسين ( عليه السلام ) و عليه دراعه سوداء و طيلسان ازرق .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Suleyman Bin Rashid, from his father who said,  ‘I saw Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws and upon himasws was a black cloak and a blue pallium’.

t: Chapter 60 – The Frankincense oil
ar: ذكرت عند ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) الادهان فذكر البنفسج و فضله فقال نعم الدهن البنفسج ادهنوا به فان فضله علي الادهان كفضلنا علي الناس و البان دهن ذكر نعم الدهن البان و انه ليعجبني الخلوق .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said,  ‘The (massaging) oils were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so the violet (oil) was mentioned, and its merits, so heasws said: ‘The best of the (massaging) oils is the violet, oil (massage) with it, for its merit over the (rest of the) oils is like ourasws merits over the (rest of the) people’. And heasws mentioned the frankincense oil: ‘The best of the oils is the frankincense, and it is Al-Khalouq which appeals to measws’.

t: Chapter 60 – The Frankincense oil
ar: شكا رجل الي ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) شقاقا في يديه و رجليه فقال له خذ قطنه فاجعل فيها بانا و ضعها في سرتك فقال اسحاق بن عمار جعلت فداك يجعل البان في قطنه و يجعلها في سرته فقال اما انت يا اسحاق فصب البان في سرتك فانها كبيره قال ابن اذينه لقيت الرجل بعد ذلك فاخبرني انه فعله مره واحده فذهب عنه .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina who said,  ‘A man complained to Abu Abdullahasws of cracks in his hands and his legs, so heasws said to him: ‘Take cotton and put some frankincense oil in it and place it in your navel’. So Is’haq Bin Ammar said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Put the frankincense oil in the cotton and make it to be in his navel?’ So heasws said: ‘As for you, O Is’haq, so pour the frankincense in your navel, for it is bigger (task)’. Ibn Azina (the narrator) said, ‘I met the man after that, so he informed me that he had done it once, so it went away from him’.

t: Chapter 60 – The Frankincense oil
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) نعم الدهن البان .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Dawood Bin Is’haq Abu Suleyman Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Al Fayz who said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The best of the (massaging) oils is the frankincense (oil)’.

t: Chapter 61 – The Lily oil
ar: قال النبي ( صلي الله عليه واله ) انه ليس شي‏ء خيرا للجسد من دهن الزنبق يعني الرازقي .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Al Sayyari, raising it, said,  ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘There is nothing better for the body than the lily oil, meaning the Jasmine flower’.

t: Chapter 61 – The Lily oil
ar: كان ابو الحسن موسي ( عليه السلام ) يستعط بالشليثا و بالزنبق الشديد الحر خسفيه قال و كان الرضا ( عليه السلام ) ايضا يستعط به فقلت لعلي بن جعفر لم ذلك فقال علي ذكرت ذلك لبعض المتطببين فذكر انه جيد للجماع .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Yaqouby, from Isa Bin Abdullah,  (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws used to sniff Al-Shaleysa (a perfume), and the lily in intense heat, (until it) dropped (drops from hisasws nose), and Al-Rezaasws as well sniffed with it’. So I said to Ali son of Ja’farasws, ‘Why is that?’ So Ali said, ‘I mentioned that to one of the physicians, so he mentioned that it is very good for the copulation’.

t: Chapter 62 – The Sesame Oil
ar: رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) كان اذا اشتكي راسه استعط بدهن الجلجلان و هو السمسم .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from someone else, from Al Khashaab, from Giyas Bin Kulyeb, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that whenever Rasool-Allahsaww complained of his head (ache), would sniff the Al-Juljulaan oil, and it is the sesame’.

t: Chapter 62 – The Sesame Oil
ar: النبي ( صلي الله عليه واله ) كان يحب ان يستعط بدهن السمسم .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, from a cousin of Al Wazaie, from Mas’ada Bin Al Yas’a, from Qays Al Bahily,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that the Prophetsaww used to love smelling the sesame oil’.

t: Chapter 63 – The Basils
ar: قال النبي ( صلي الله عليه واله ) اذا اتي احدكم بريحان فليشمه و ليضعه علي عينيه فانه من الجنه و اذا اتي احدكم به فلا يرده .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Talha Bin Zayd, from the one who raised it, said,  ‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘Whenever one of you is brought the basil, so let him smell it and place it upon his eyes, for it is from the Paradise, and whenever one of you is brought it, so let him not reject it’.

t: Chapter 63 – The Basils
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) اذا اتي احدكم بالريحان فليشمه و ليضعه علي عينيه فانه من الجنه .
en: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Whenever one of you is brought the basil, so let him smell it, and let him place it upon his eyes, for it is from the Paradise’.

t: Chapter 63 – The Basils
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) الريحان واحد و عشرون نوعا سيدها الاس .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The basil is of twenty one types, the chief of it is the myrtle’.

t: Chapter 63 – The Basils
ar: دخلت علي ابي عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) و في يده مخضبه فيها ريحان .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,  ‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws and in hisasws hand was a dyeing-box wherein was basil’.

t: Chapter 63 – The Basils
ar: دخلت علي ابي الحسن صاحب العسكر ( عليه السلام ) فجاء صبي من صبيانه فناوله ورده فقبلها و وضعها علي عينيه ثم ناولنيها و قال يا ابا هاشم من تناول ورده او ريحانه فقبلها و وضعها علي عينيه ثم صلي علي محمد و ال محمد الايمه كتب الله له الحسنات مثل رمل عالج و محا عنه من السييات مثل ذلك .
en: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, form Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said,  ‘I went over to Abu Al Hassanasws the owner of the army (Saahib Al-Askarasws), so there came a child from hisasws children and gave him a rose. So heasws kissed it and placed it upon hisasws eyes, then gave it to me and said: ‘O Abu Hashim! The one who grabs a rose or basil should kiss it and place it upon his eyes, then send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, the Imamsasws, Allahazwj would Write for him the rewards similar to the sands of the wilderness, and delete the sins from him similar to that’.

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: من السعاده سعه المنزل .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘From the happiness is the spaciousness of the home’.

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: ان ابا الحسن ( عليه السلام ) اشتري دارا و امر مولي له ان يتحول اليها و قال ان منزلك ضيق فقال قد احدث هذه الدار ابي فقال ابو الحسن ( عليه السلام ) ان كان ابوك احمق ينبغي ان تكون مثله .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said,  ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws bought a house and ordered a slave of hisasws that he transfers to it and said: ‘Your home is narrow’. So he said, ‘My father had built the house’. So Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘If your father was stupid is it befitting that you become similar to him?’

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: ثلاثه للمومن فيها راحه دار واسعه تواري عورته و سوء حاله من الناس و امراه صالحه تعينه علي امر الدنيا و الاخره و ابنه او اخت يخرجها من منزله اما بموت او بتزوج .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Saeed Bin Janah, from Mutarraf, a slave of Ma’an,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There are three (things) which are a best for the Believer – a spacious house to cover his nakedness and his evil state with from the people, and a righteous woman supporting him upon the affairs of the world and the Hereafter, and a daughter or a sister exiting her from his home either when he dies or by getting her married off’.

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: سمعت ابا الحسن ( عليه السلام ) يقول العيش السعه في المنازل و الفضل في الخدم .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from his father, from Bashir who said,  ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassanasws saying: ‘The good life is in the spaciousness of the home, and the graciousness regarding the servants’.

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: ابا الحسن ( عليه السلام ) سيل عن فضل عيش الدنيا قال سعه المنزل و كثره المحبين .
en: From him, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Saeed, from someone else,  ‘Abu Al-Hassanasws was asked about the gracious living of the world. Heasws said: ‘Spaciousness of the home and the abundance of those that love you’.

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: من شقاء العيش ضيق المنزل .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Ali Bin Abu Al Mugheira,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘From a miserable living, is a narrow home’.

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) من سعاده المرء المسلم المسكن الواسع .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘From happiness of the Muslim person is the spacious dwelling’.

t: Chapter 64 – Spaciousness of the home
ar: شكا رجل من الانصار الي رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ان الدور قد اكتنفته فقال النبي ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ارفع صوتك ما استطعت و سل الله ان يوسع عليك .
en: And by this chain, said,  ‘A man from the helpers complained to Rasool-Allahsaww that the houses had congested him. So the Prophetsaww said: ‘Raise your voice as much as you can and ask Allahazwj that Heazwj Makes it spacious for you’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) اتاني جبرييل و قال يا محمد ان ربك يقريك السلام و ينهي عن تزويق البيوت قال ابو بصير فقلت ما تزويق البيوت فقال تصاوير التماثيل .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Jibraeelas came unto mesaww and said: ‘O Muhammadsaww! Yoursaww Lordazwj Conveys the Greetings and Forbids from decorating the houses’. Abu Baseer said, ‘So I said, ‘What is the decoration of the houses?’ So heasws said: ‘Pictures and the statues’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ان جبرييل ( عليه السلام ) اتاني فقال انا معاشر الملايكه لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب و لا تمثال جسد و لا اناء يبال فيه .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Bin Marwan,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Jibraeelas came unto mesaww, so heas said: ‘We, the group of Angels neither enter a house in which is a dog, nor any statue of a body, nor a utensil in which is urine’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: ان جبرييل ( عليه السلام ) قال انا لا ندخل بيتا فيه صوره و لا كلب يعني صوره الانسان و لا بيتا فيه تماثيل .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Baseer,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Jibraeelas said: ‘We (the Angels) neither enter a house in which there is a picture, nor a dog, meaning pictures of the humans, nor a house wherein are statues’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: من مثل تمثالا كلف يوم القيامه ان ينفخ فيه الروح .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from a man,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who carves a statue would be brought on the Day of Judgement (in front of the carving) and he (the carver will be asked to) blow the spirit into it (to bring it to life)’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: ان عليا ( عليه السلام ) كره الصوره في البيوت .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Musna,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said that Aliasws disliked the pictures in the houses’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: سالته عن الوساده و البساط يكون فيه التماثيل فقال لا باس به يكون في البيت قلت التماثيل فقال كل شي‏ء يوطا فلا باس به .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the pillows and the rugs wherein happen to be the resemblances. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it if it happens to be in the house’. I said, ‘The resemblances?’ Heasws said: ‘Everything which is trampled, so there is no problem with it’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: الله عز و جل يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب و تماثيل فقال و الله ما هي تماثيل الرجال و النساء و لكنها الشجر و شبهه .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [34:13] They made for him whatsoever he desired of Prayer Niches, and images. So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! These were not images of the men and the women, but these were the trees and the likes of it’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: لا باس بان يكون التماثيل في البيوت اذا غيرت رءوسها منها و ترك ما سوي ذلك .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara Bin Ayn,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘There is no problem if there happen to be the resemblances in the houses when its heads are changed from it and it is left, what is besides that’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: سالته عن الدار و الحجره فيها التماثيل ا يصلي فيها فقال لا تصل فيها و فيها شي‏ء يستقبلك الا ان لا تجد بدا فتقطع رءوسها و الا فلا تصل فيها .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali,  (It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’farasws, from Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the house and the chamber wherein are the resemblances, can one Pray in it?’ So heasws said: ‘Do not Pray in it and therein is something facing you, except if it is inevitable then you can cut-off its heads, or else do not Pray in it’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) ثلاثه معذبون يوم القيامه رجل كذب في روياه يكلف ان يعقد بين شعيرتين و ليس بعاقد بينهما و رجل صور تماثيل يكلف ان ينفخ فيها و ليس بنافخ .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, altogether from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysmi, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar who said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Three would be Punished on the Day of Judgement – a man who lied regarding his dream, he would be Encumbered to tie a knot between two grains, and he would not be able to tie a knot between the two; and a man who images resemblances, he would be Encumbered that he blows (a spirit) into it, and he would not be able to blow into it’. (P.s. – the description of the third is missing).

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) بعثني رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) في هدم القبور و كسر الصور .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww sent measws regarding the demolishing of the graves and breaking of the pictures’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: قال جبرييل ( عليه السلام ) يا رسول الله انا لا ندخل بيتا فيه صوره انسان و لا بيتا يبال فيه و لا بيتا فيه كلب .
en: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Amro Bin Khalid,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Jibraeelas said: ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! We (Angels) neither enter a house wherein is a picture of a human, nor a house which has been urinated in, nor a house in which is a dog’.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) قال جبرييل ( عليه السلام ) انا لا ندخل بيتا فيه تمثال لا يوطا . الحديث مختصر .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kindy,  (It has been narrated) from his father, and he was in charge of providing water for the ablution for Amir Al-Momineenasws, said, ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Jibraeelas said: ‘We (Angels) neither enter a house wherein are resemblances not trampled’. The Hadeeth is shortened.

t: Chapter 65 – Decorating of the houses
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) بعثني رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) الي المدينه فقال لا تدع صوره الا محوتها و لا قبرا الا سويته و لا كلبا الا قتلته .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww sent measws to Al-Medina, so hesaww said: ‘Neither leave any picture except delete it, nor any grave except even it, nor a dog except kill it’.

t: Chapter 66 – Masonry of the construction
ar: ان الله عز و جل وكل ملكا بالبناء يقول لمن رفع سقفا فوق ثمانيه اذرع اين تريد يا فاسق .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Fazl Al Nowfaly, from Ziyad Bin Amro Al Ju’fy, from the one who narrated it,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Allocated an Angel with the construction, saying to the one who raises a roof above eighty cubits: ‘Where are you intending (to go to), O wicked one?’

t: Chapter 66 – Masonry of the construction
ar: اذا كان سمك البيت فوق سبعه اذرع او قال ثمانيه اذرع فكان ما فوق السبع و الثمان الاذرع محتضرا و قال بعضهم مسكونا .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, and someone else,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the ceiling of the room is above seven cubits’, or said: ‘eight cubits, what is above the seven and the eight cubits is a meeting place’, and some of them said, ‘Heasws said: ‘A dwelling (for Satanla)’’.

t: Chapter 66 – Masonry of the construction
ar: شكا اليه رجل عبث اهل الارض باهل بيته و بعياله فقال كم سقف بيتك فقال عشره اذرع فقال اذرع ثمانيه اذرع ثم اكتب ايه الكرسي فيما بين الثمانيه الي العشره كما تدور فان كل بيت سمكه اكثر من ثمانيه اذرع فهو محتضر تحضره الجن يكون فيه مسكنه .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Muhammad Al Ansary, from Aban Bin Usman,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘A man complained to himasws of the bad treatment of the people of the land with his family and his children. So heasws said: ‘How much (height) is the ceiling of your house’. So heasws said: ‘Ten cubits’. So heasws said : ‘Measure out eight cubits, then write the Verse of the Chair [2:255] in what is between the eight to the ten, just as you go around. So in each of the rooms, it its ceiling is higher than eight cubits, so it is a meeting place, the Jinn being present in it, and in it would become its dwelling’.

t: Chapter 66 – Masonry of the construction
ar: في سمك البيت اذا رفع ثمانيه اذرع كان مسكونا فاذا زاد علي ثمانيه فليكتب علي راس الثمان ايه الكرسي .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, and Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, altogether from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding a ceiling of the house when it is raised to eight cubits, it would be a dwelling. So when it exceeds eight, so let him write at the top of the eight, the Verse of the Chair [2:255]’.

t: Chapter 66 – Masonry of the construction
ar: شكا رجل الي ابي جعفر ( عليه السلام ) و قال اخرجتنا الجن عن منازلنا فقال اجعلوا سقوف بيوتكم سبعه اذرع و اجعلوا الحمام في اكناف الدار قال الرجل ففعلنا ذلك فما راينا شييا نكرهه بعد ذلك .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hamza Bin Humran who said,  ‘A man complained to Abu Ja’farasws and said: ‘The Jinn have made us to exit our house’. So heasws said: ‘Make the ceilings of our houses of seven cubits, and make the bathroom in the fringes of the house’. The man said, ‘So we did that and we did not see anything we disliked after that’.

t: Chapter 66 – Masonry of the construction
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) ابن بيتك سبعه اذرع فما كان فوق ذلك سكنه الشياطين ان الشياطين ليست في السماء و لا في الارض و انما تسكن الهواء .
en: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Al Husayn Bin Zurara, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Build your house up to seven cubits, so whatever is above that, the Satansla would dwell in it. The Satansla are neither in the sky nor in the ground, but rather they dwell in the atmosphere’.

t: Chapter 66 – Masonry of the construction
ar: اذا كان البيت فوق ثمانيه اذرع فاكتب في اعلاه ايه الكرسي .
en: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and Muhsan Bin Ahmad, from Aban Bin Usman, form Muhammad Bin Ismail,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the house is above eight cubits, so write in its upper part the Verse of the Chair [2:255]’.

t: Chapter 67 – The Roof Enclosure
ar: نهي رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ان يبات علي سطح غير محجر .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade to sleep upon the roof other than in an enclosure (boundary wall)’.

t: Chapter 67 – The Roof Enclosure
ar: قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) من بات علي سطح غير محجر فاصابه شي‏ء فلا يلومن الا نفسه .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ali Bin Is’haq, from Sahl Bin Al Yas’a,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who sleeps upon a roof without an enclosure (boundary wall), so something hits him, so he should not blame any except for himself’.

t: Chapter 67 – The Roof Enclosure
ar: ه كره ان يبيت الرجل علي سطح ليست عليه حجره و الرجل و المراه في ذلك سواء .
en: From him, from Al Hajjal, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having dislike that the man should sleep upon a roof and there is not enclosure upon it, and the man and the woman with regards to that, are the same’.

t: Chapter 67 – The Roof Enclosure
ar: ه كره البيتوته للرجل علي سطح وحده او علي سطح ليست عليه حجره و الرجل و المراه فيه بمنزله .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having disliked for the man to spend the night alone upon a roof, or upon a rood with no enclosure upon it, and the man and the woman with regards to it are at the same status’.

t: Chapter 67 – The Roof Enclosure
ar: السطح يبات عليه و هو غير محجر قال يجزيه ان يكون مقدار ارتفاع الحايط ذراعين .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza and someone else,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the roof one sleeps upon and he is not enclosed (by the boundary wall), heasws said: ‘It would suffice for him if there happened to be a wall of a height of the measurement of two cubits’.

t: Chapter 67 – The Roof Enclosure
ar: سالت ابا عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) عن السطح ينام عليه بغير حجره قال نهي رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) عن ذلك فسالته عن ثلاثه حيطان فقال لا الا اربعه قلت كم طول الحايط قال اقصره ذراع و شبر .
en: From him, from his father, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,  ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the roof, can one sleep upon it without an enclosure?’ Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from that’. So I asked himasws about three walls, so heasws said: ‘No, unless it is four’. I said, ‘How much should the height of the walls be?’ Heasws said: ‘The shortest of it is one cubit and one open-palms width (Shibr)’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: من مر العيش النقله من دار الي دار و اكل خبز الشري .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Sayyari, from a sheykh from his companions, from the one who mentioned it,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘From the bitterness of the living is the transferring from a house to a house and eating the bitter bread’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: من كسب مالا من غير حله سلط الله عليه البناء و الماء و الطين .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who gathers wealth from other than Permissible means, Allahazwj would Cause him to be overcome by the construction, and the water, and the clay’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: رايت ابا الحسن موسي ( عليه السلام ) و قد بني بمني بناء ثم هدمه .
en: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Usman who said,  ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws and heasws had built a construction at Mina, then demolished it’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: سالته عن قول الله عز و جل و ان من شي‏ء الا يسبح بحمده و لكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم قال تنقض الجدر تسبيحها .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Dawood Al Raqy,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [17:44] and there is not a single thing but it Glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their Glorification. Heasws said: ‘The cracking of the wall is its Glorification’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: قال ابو عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) اكنسوا افنيتكم و لا تشبهوا باليهود .
en: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,  ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Sweep your courtyards and do not resemble the Jews’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) لا توووا التراب خلف الباب فانه ماوي الشياطين .
en: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, raising it, said,  ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Do not accumulate the dust behind the door, for it is a shelter of the Satansla’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: كل بناء ليس بكفاف فهو وبال علي صاحبه يوم القيامه .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abu Jameela, from Humeyd Al Sayrafi,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Every construction without a boundary, so it would have bad consequences for its owner on the Day of Judgement’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: كنس البيت ينفي الفقر .
en: From him, from one of his companions,  (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Sweeping the house negates the poverty’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: نهي رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) ان يدخل بيتا مظلما الا بمصباح .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from entering a dark house except with a lantern’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: شكت اسافل الحيطان الي الله عز و جل من ثقل اعاليها فاوحي الله عز و جل اليها يحمل بعضكم بعضا .
en: From him, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moala, from Ibrahim Bin Al Khataab,  (It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The bottom part of the wall complained to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic from the weight of its upper part. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto it bear each other’s weight’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: قال امير المومنين ( عليه السلام ) قال رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) بيت الشياطين من بيوتكم بيت العنكبوت .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khataab, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun, from Isa Bin Abdullah, from his grandfather who said,  ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The house of Satansla from your houses is the house of the spider (cobweb)’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: سالت ابا عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) عن اغلاق الابواب و ايكاء الاواني و اطفاء السراج فقال اغلق بابك فان الشيطان لا يفتح بابا و اطف السراج من الفويسقه و هي الفاره لا تحرق بيتك و اوك الاناء . و روي ان الشيطان لا يكشف مخمرا يعني مغطي .
en: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,  ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about closing the doors, and covering the utensils, and extinguishing the lantern, so heasws said: ‘Close your door for the Satanla does not open a door, and extinguish your lantern from the rats, and it is the mouse which would not (be able to) burn down your house and overturn your utensils’.  And it is reported that, ‘(Heasws said): ‘The Satanla does not uncover a lid, meaning a covering’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: قال الرضا ( عليه السلام ) اسراج السراج قبل ان تغيب الشمس ينفي الفقر .
en: Abu Ali Al Ashary, raising it, said,  ‘Al-Rezaasws said: ‘Igniting the lantern before the sun sets negates the poverty’.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: كان النبي ( صلي الله عليه واله ) اذا خرج في الصيف من البيت خرج يوم الخميس و اذا اراد ان يدخل في الشتاء من البرد دخل يوم الجمعه و روي ايضا كان دخوله و خروجه ليله الجمعه .
en: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whenever the Prophetsaww went out in the summer, went out on the day of Thursday, and whenever hesaww wanted to enter in the winter from the cold, entered on the day of Friday’. And it has been reported as well that hissaww entry and hissaww exit was on the night of Friday.

t: Chapter 68 – The Miscellaneous
ar: روي ابو هاشم الجعفري عن ابي الحسن الثالث ( عليه السلام ) قال ان الله عز و جل جعل من ارضه بقاعا تسمي المرحومات احب ان يدعي فيها فيجيب و ان الله عز و جل جعل من ارضه بقاعا تسمي المنتقمات فاذا كسب الرجل مالا من غير حله سلط الله عليه بقعه منها فانفقه فيها .
en: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah who said,  ‘Abu Hisham Al-Ja’fary reported from Abu Al-Hassanasws the 3rd having said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Made from Hisazwj earth a spot called Al-Marhoumaat. Iasws would love it to supplicate therein for it would be Answered; and that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Made from Hisazwj earth a spot called Al-Muntaqimaat, so whenever the man amasses wealth from other than Permissible means, Allahazwj Causes a spot from it to overcome him, so its gets spent therein’.

t: Chapter 69 – Abhorrence for the human being to sleep alone, and the characteristics Prohibited about it for the reason of fearfulness
ar: نزلت علي ابي جعفر ( عليه السلام ) فقال يا ميمون من يرقد معك بالليل ا معك غلام قلت لا قال فلا تنم وحدك فان اجرا ما يكون الشيطان علي الانسان اذا كان وحده .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Qaddah, from his father who said,  ‘I lodged at Abu Ja’farasws, so heasws said: ‘O Maymoun! Who would slumber along with you at night, is there a slave with you?’ I said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘So do not sleep alone, for the most audacious that the Satanla can become, does so upon the human being when he was alone’.

t: Chapter 69 – Abhorrence for the human being to sleep alone, and the characteristics Prohibited about it for the reason of fearfulness
ar: من تخلي علي قبر او بال قايما او بال في ماء قايما او مشي في حذاء واحد او شرب قايما او خلا في بيت وحده و بات علي غمر فاصابه شي‏ء من الشيطان لم يدعه الا ان يشاء الله و اسرع ما يكون الشيطان الي الانسان و هو علي بعض هذه الحالات فان رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) خرج في سريه فاتي وادي مجنه فنادي اصحابه الا لياخذ كل رجل منكم بيد صاحبه و لا يدخلن رجل وحده و لا يمضي رجل وحده قال فتقدم رجل وحده فانتهي اليه و قد صرع فاخبر بذلك رسول الله ( صلي الله عليه واله ) فاخذ بابهامه فغمزها ثم قال بسم الله اخرج خبيث انا رسول الله قال فقام .
en: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The one who defecates upon a grave or urinates standing, or urinates in water standing, or walks in one shoe, or drinks standing, or isolates himself alone in a house, and sleeps upon dripping hands (from food stains), so something from the Satanla hits him, it would not leave him except if Allahazwj so Desires it, and the quickest of what the Satanla comes upon the human being is when he is upon one of these states.  Rasool-Allahsaww went out in a military brigade, so hesaww came to a valley of the Jinn. So hesaww called out to hissaww companions: ‘Let each man from you grab the hand of his companions, and no man should enter alone, nor should a man go past it alone’.  Heasws said: ‘So a man went forward alone and ended up to it, and he had epileptic fits. So Rasool-Allahsaww was informed with that, so hesaww grabbed with his thumb and touched him, then said: ‘In the Name of Allahazwj! Get out, Wicked one, Isaww am Rasool-Allahsaww!’ Heasws said: ‘So he stood up’.

t: Chapter 69 – Abhorrence for the human being to sleep alone, and the characteristics Prohibited about it for the reason of fearfulness
ar: قال ان الشيطان اشد ما يهم بالانسان حين يكون وحده خاليا لا اري ان يرقد وحده .
en: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,  (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘The Satanla is the most troublesome with the human being when he happens to be alone, isolated. Iasws should not see him sleeping alone’.

t: Chapter 69 – Abhorrence for the human being to sleep alone, and the characteristics Prohibited about it for the reason of fearfulness
ar: سالت ابا عبد الله ( عليه السلام ) عن الرجل يبيت في بيت وحده فقال اني لاكره ذلك و ان اضطر الي ذلك فلا باس و لكن يكثر ذكر الله في منامه ما استطاع .
